classification.difficultyReason: Use the explicitly obtuse inverse-sine branch, then angle sum and compass orientation to obtain a bearing.

content.prompt:
Yorker ($Y$) is 134 km due east of Vendor ($V$).
Xena ($X$) is on a bearing of $232^\circ$ from Yorker and is also 85 km from Vendor.
$\angle VXY$ is an obtuse angle. Find the bearing of Xena from Vendor.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle VYX &= 270^\circ-232^\circ=38^\circ \\
\frac{\sin\angle VXY}{134} &= \frac{\sin38^\circ}{85} \\
\sin\angle VXY &= \frac{134\sin38^\circ}{85}
\end{align*}$$
$\angle VXY$ is obtuse.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle VXY &= 180^\circ-\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{134\sin38^\circ}{85}\right) \\
\angle YVX &= 180^\circ-38^\circ-\angle VXY \\
\text{Bearing} &= 90^\circ+\angle YVX \\
&\approx 128^\circ
\end{align*}$$
